title: path traversal
body:
(file/folder names): Used in path.join and FS operations (new-file-command.ts, new-folder-command.ts, rename-command.ts).

Result: FAIL. Input is not validated or sanitized before use in file system paths. Potential for path traversal (../../something).

Severity: ERROR

File: packages/vscode/src/commands/new-file-command.ts, new-folder-command.ts, rename-command.ts

Rule Violated: input.IS_SANITIZED_BEFORE(sensitive_sink) (Conceptual Sink: fs operations)

Details: User input from showInputBox used for file/folder names is not sanitized. Malicious input (e.g., containing ../) could lead to path traversal and writing/deleting files outside the intended directory. Input must be strictly validated against allowed characters and path manipulation attempts.

Clipboard content (apply-changes-command.ts): Parsed for file paths (parse_clipboard_multiple_files), paths used in FS operations (vscode.workspace.fs.*, fs.*).

Result: FAIL. File paths extracted from clipboard content are used directly in file system operations without validation or sanitization. Potential for path traversal or writing outside the workspace if clipboard contains crafted malicious paths.

Severity: ERROR

File: packages/vscode/src/commands/apply-changes-command/apply-changes-command.ts (functions replace_files_directly, create_file_if_needed)

Rule Violated: input.IS_SANITIZED_BEFORE(sensitive_sink) (Conceptual Sink: fs operations using paths from clipboard)

Details: File paths parsed from clipboard content via parse_clipboard_multiple_files are used in FS operations without sanitization, risking path traversal. Paths must be validated to ensure they are within the workspace and do not contain traversal sequences.

title: Firefox extension didn't work for me.
body:
This might have been user error, or it might have been complications with my Firefox setup, but when I tried using the Firefox extension, the VSCode extension would open the page, but then nothing else happened; no interaction on the web page.  I use Firefox extensively, practically exclusively, and have an elaborate setup on it. I did make sure I only had the Firefox extension installed on my last few attempts.

The chrome extension seems to be working as expected.  I use chrome only for google stuff, and I have a very, very simple setup on it.
author: GaxGuy

comments.body: Hi, it's been fixed today (0.1.39). Please confirm if this version is fine for you.

There are several security issues in the VSCode extension that can be resolved by setting up dependabot scanning and CodeQL scanning and implementing the automatic security updates.  I hope you will set those up.  I haven't looked specifically, but some resolutions might be more involved than automatic security updates.  

I'm going to avoid using extensions that relate to API keys that have these sorts of security issues.  Therefor I'm unwilling to check the Firefox extension while these security issues are present.

Hi, I want this package be as secure as possible so you can trust it. Is there anything other than very popular npm packages outdated by a minor version? I set up dependabot so it will be covered. If you can, please provide some advice what else can be done.

I'm using only few dependencies and all are well established what is the most important thing.
Regarding API keys: these are not required for web chats initializations. It's a 100% local process. When providing API keys, you're the one making requests directly to the provider's endpoint.

> Hi, I want this package be as secure as possible so you can trust it. Is there anything other than very popular npm packages outdated by a minor version? I set up dependabot so it will be covered. If you can, please provide some advice what else can be done.
> 
> I'm using only few dependencies and all are well established what is the most important thing.

I'm glad to hear you're concerned about code security.  I've had weird encounters with other repositories that have easily detectable and solvable security vulnerabilities and their approach is to simply ignore them.  It's so strange.

I think you setup dependabot auto dependency updating only, as far as I can tell.

dependabot code scanning is separate from dependabot dependency updates.

CodeQL code scanning is also separate from both of those

All three types of automation are free for public repositories, and relatively easy to setup, especially for projects that don't have complex build steps.  They are all under Settings, in Advanced Security - the other two are nearby where you setup the dependency updating.

For dependabot code scanning; it can try to create resolutions to security issues it finds.  Sometimes updating a dependency version is more involved than just changing the version numbers because the typescript ecology is extremely ossified, with long dependency chains ossified at versions that were already 6 months to a year out of date when they were ossified in in the first place, which required older out of date dependencies, which themselves required older out of date dependencies, and so on.

Dependabot code scanning can sometimes go through al that and resolve a dependency chain update that doesn't have known vulnerabilities.  Dependabot dependency updating alone won't do that. That's why I did a pull request with several security updates incorporated with it too.   I should have kept the dependabot dependency updating separate from those - that was a matter of my inexperience with collaborating on github.  You might have noticed that one of the commits in my pull request had something like 366 lines modified, or whatever it was.  That wasn't an elaborate random number generator; it had purpose.

CodeQL separately will scan for _different_ issues than dependabot code scanning.  Usually there will be an option for Copilot to try to generate a resolution to issues that CodeQL discovered.  Sometimes they are simple and you just look at them and apply them, sometimes they require very careful observation about the implications of the code change.  My pull request might have included 1 or more Copilot auto-generated resolutions to vulnerabilities discovered by CodeQL; I don't recall for sure.

There might be other code scanning tools that are also available for free - I'm not sure - some I've looked at were free trials, or related to paid services.

Either way; dependabot code scanning and CodeQL sure are good starts. and for issues reported you can obviously develop your own resolution if you want, try to get them to develop a resolution automatically (which is probably about 60% to 85% likely), and modify that if you want or just use it directly.

If I'm mistaken and you've already setup all three, then maybe this can be helpful to anybody else that reads it.

But I've noticed that there are very, very many security vulnerabilities all throughout the typescript/javascript ecology, which could interact to prove a climbable vulnerability surface leading to potential for exploitations far beyond what a single vulnerability seems to offer, and the ossification, abandonment, and continued use of abandoned packages in new developments is seriously magnifying and spreading the problem.

Some of these packages that are in widespread use in the ecology have _dozens_ of separate security vulnerabilities each, and many of them haven't been modified in 6 months to several years.

title: Save selection does not auto populates file.
body:
Expected behavior for saving selection to a file:
- First it's going to check if file has correct schema
- If it is then it's going to append current selection to file and write all file paths and probably prompt user to write recognizable name for this selection
- If file does not exist it is both created and added to .gitignore
- There is additional interface to easily delete selections by their recognizable name.
